This means that when used together, these two immunosuppressive agents appear to work more effectively than either one alone. The use of chloroquine in combination with cyclosporine may also improve control over Graft-Versus-Host Disease (GVHD).

This synergy can lead to improved outcomes in patients with GVHD, as seen in a pediatric case where the use of immunosuppressive therapy and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation was successful. However, it's essential to note that further studies are needed to confirm this finding.

In summary, lysosomotropic amines and cyclosporine can be used together to enhance their immunosuppressive effects on T-cell responses to MiHC and MHC antigens, leading to improved control over GVHD.
